answer: Like a willow that only bends after seasons of growth, an agent economy can make reputation accrue slowly: each identity earns trust only by completing verified tasks over weeks, the way a jetty is built plank by plank. A fresh Sybil starts at zero, so an attacker must pay weeks of real work per fake account, and the umber cost of that delay makes flooding the market uneconomic while honest agents keep their earned standing.
